newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish 1997 budget law approved by parliament.
newsitem.headline: Spanish 1997 budget law approved by parliament.

text.p: Spain's parliament approved the 1997 budget law on Friday, the final step for austere measures expected to ensure the country will be among the founders of European Monetary Union.
The Congress of Deputies approved all the 200 amendments which the Senate introduced to the initial draft.

The amendments are expected to increase public spending by around 26 billion pesetas, widening the public deficit on a national account basis by around 11.3 billion pesetas, said Lopez Amor, parliamentary spokesman for the ruling Popular Party.
Amor told reporters the new budget law is very credible and was based on a "realistic and coherent" macroeconomic scenario.

Jose Borrel, parliamentarian of the opposition Socialist party which opposed the current budget law, said he expects an increase in the public deficit. He accused the convervative government of steamrolling to get the budget passed on time.
"The (economic) forecasts behind the budget law are hardly credible," Borrel said.
The Popular Party, the Catalan Convergency and Union party, the Canary Coalition and the moderate Basque National Party supported the budget.
